_comment: Interface messages. To add a language, copy this file under a new code and translate the values. Do not change the keys. {} is a placeholder.
links_found: links carried over from the book: {}
meta_unknown: WARNING: unknown keys in the instructions header: {0}. Understood keys: {1}. The title and author in the target language are title_target and author_target.
no_head_plain: no headings: the book is split by word count at paragraph boundaries. Normal for continuous prose.
stop_no_head: STOP: no headings found, although the format carries markup.
stop_no_text: STOP: almost no text — {} paragraphs, {} words.
stop_same_lang: STOP: the text is already in the target language ({:.0%} of lines).
same_lang_hint: Nothing to translate. If the book does contain foreign-language passages, run with --force-translate.
nothing_translate: everything was translated earlier ({} chunks), nothing to do
nothing_edit: everything was edited earlier ({} chunks), nothing to do
no_text_hint: This looks like a comic, an art album or a picture book: the text lives inside the images. The pipeline cannot translate that.
no_head_hint: The markup most likely was not recognised, so chunking will fall back to word counts and cut the book mid-scene or between narrators. Translating it in this state is pointless.
no_head_fix_file: 1. Open {0} and look for a style marked "p" where it should be "title". Fix it by hand, delete book.json, run again.
no_head_fix_redo: 2. Or delete {0} and redo detection: ./booktrans BOOK --only structure
no_head_fix_force: 3. If the book really has no chapters, run it with --no-headings
digest_kept: digest refused ({0}) — keeping the previous one
scout_done_already: scouting already done (delete work/scout.md to redo it)
scout_big: WARNING: the reference is oversized and goes into every translation request. Trim {0} by hand, or delete it and redo the scouting pass.
shr_long: the answer is no shorter than the original ({0} chars)
shr_short: the answer is under half of what was asked ({0} instead of {1})
scout_condense: reference too big: {0} chars instead of {1}, condensing ...
scout_condense_no: condensing rejected: {0} of {1} rows lost — keeping the original
preview_left: PREVIEW: {0} blocks left in the source language
sources_head: QUOTATIONS FROM OTHER TRANSLATIONS — {0}, need checking
sources_hint: Check these against the edition: the machine cannot confirm the text came from the source rather than from memory.
usage_note_scout: Scouting and markup detection are not included: they write no chunk files.
usage_note_sub: On a subscription the sum is indicative: this is what API rates would cost.
qa1_dropped: the source lost {0} pieces ({1} words) on the way into the book — the table of contents and running heads are dropped on purpose
qa1_undone: the layout pass threw away {0} pieces that do not look like waste — the mark was undone and the text kept
qa2: 2. NUMBERS  (digits in the source must stay digits)
qa2_ocr: a digit standing for a letter (1 for I, 5 for S) — OCR damage, not counted: blocks {0}
qa2_new: digits that were not in the source appeared in the translation — blocks: {0} (nothing to check them against, take a look)
qa2_word: a number glued to a word ("88-page", "2-D") — the other language writes it differently, not counted: blocks {0}
qa2_si: a measure converted to SI ("165 pounds" -> "75 kg") — not counted: blocks {0}
qa2_sup: a power the OCR flattened and the translation restored ("1031" -> "10<sup>31</sup>") — not counted: blocks {0}
qa3: 3. PARAGRAPH LENGTH  (an outlier betrays an omission)
qa3_mid: usual length ratio for this book: {0}
qa4_bad: blocks in the source script: {0} (names and titles are usually fine)
qa4_skip: skipped: source and target use the same script ({0})
qa5: 5. FOOTNOTE REFERENCES  (the number must survive translation)
qa5_bad: ERROR: {0} of {1} references lost — the note will sit at the end of the book with nothing pointing to it:
qa_total: TOTAL remarks: {0}   (blocking ones are sections 1, 2, 5 and 6)
prompt_lost: WARNING: protocol tokens missing from it: {0}. The parser looks for exactly those — footnotes, digest and terms will vanish without a sound.
no_fingerprint: some finished chunks come from an older version: there is nothing to check them against, so they are taken on trust. To redo them for certain, delete work/tr and work/ed
pdf_failed: the build failed; the source {0} and the error log are beside it
pdf_no_engine: {0} is ready but there is nothing to build it with: {1} is needed. Install it (on Debian and Ubuntu the package is texlive-luatex) and run: lualatex {0}
lim_known: {0} is rate-limited for about {1} min more — skipping
lim_wait: rate limit reached, waiting {0} min (waited {1} min so far)
probe_dead: {0} does not answer even a trivial question: the chunk is fine, the access is not — waiting
notes_already: notes were processed earlier ({0} chunks), nothing to do
lim_gave_up: rate limits did not recover within {0} h: {1}
h_desc: Translate a book in a single run (target set by --to)
h_epilog:
examples:
  ./booktrans book.epub --to en
  ./booktrans book.pdf -p glossary.md -o Book.fb2 --to en
  ./booktrans book.epub --only translate --chunks 5,6,7
  ./booktrans book.epub --agent cmd --agent-cmd 'llm -s {system}'

the instructions file (-p) may start with a header:
  ---
  title_target: Usurpation
  author_target: Sue Burke
  series: Semiosis
  series_no: 3
  ---
  ...then free text: what to call the characters, which terms to fix...
h_book: epub, fb2, html, pdf or txt
h_check: check that everything needed is installed, then exit
doc_opt: optional — needed only for the formats you use
doc_opt_bad: optional and missing: {0}. epub, fb2 and txt work regardless
doc_pdftohtml: the links of a pdf: index, notes, addresses
doc_pdfimages: pictures out of pdf (same poppler package)
doc_charset: rare txt encodings; the common ones are detected without it
doc_agent: the {0} agent: it is what translates the book, nothing works without it
doc_agent_how: install the "{0}" agent CLI and sign in to it once
doc_tex: building a pdf from the LaTeX output; the .tex itself needs none of it
doc_prompts: prompts are taken from here, top down (your own survive an upgrade):
doc_bad: required and missing: {0}. The minus lines above say what to install and how
h_profile: profile: a file of command-line keys (a name from profiles/ or a path); an explicit key beats the profile
prof_nofile: no profile {0}. Looked for it by name in: {1}
prof_nested: profile {0} contains --profile: a profile inside a profile is not expanded
h_prompt: file of instructions for the translator
h_prompt_text: instructions for the translator as a string (may be combined with -p)
prompt_nofile: no such instructions file: {0}. If you meant a string of instructions, the option for that is --prompt-text.
h_out: output file: fb2, epub, html, txt, tex or pdf (next to the source by default)
inject_found: WARNING: the book addresses the translating machine — {0} places
inject_hint: This is not a retelling or an example: the instruction is aimed at whoever processes the book. The model has nothing to carry it out with — tools are off — but it can steer the translation. Look at these places in the original.
inject_stop: STOPPED before translating. Looked into it and still want to translate — run with --force-injected.
h_force_injected: translate even if the book addresses the translating machine
h_force_edit: keep editing even if the model stalls on three chunks in a row
h_model: model for every pass; comma-separated for fallbacks on refusal, colon for another agent: model,claude:other
h_scout: scouting model, a comma-separated chain (defaults to --model)
h_translator: translation model, a comma-separated chain (defaults to --model)
h_editor: editing and footnotes model, a comma-separated chain (defaults to --model)
h_ocrfixer: model that repairs OCR damage in the source, a comma-separated chain (defaults to the cheapest of the chosen agent)
h_formatter: model for working out the markup — epub and fb2 styles, pdf and txt pieces; a comma-separated chain (defaults to the cheapest of the chosen agent)
code_known: listings already processed: {0} (delete work/code.json to redo)
code_failed: listings not processed: {0} — their comments stay in the source language
h_code: what to do with listings: comments — translate the comments in them (default), asis — leave them alone
regrown: paragraphs re-asked for a length that did not match: {0}
ocr_made: the pdf text layer came from OCR ({0}) — the passes are warned of the damage
ocr_seen: recognition damage shows in the text: {0}
fix_known: recognition damage already corrected: {0} fixes (delete work/ocrfix.json to redo)
fix_failed: blocks not processed: {0} — the damage in them stays
marks_known: text already marked up (delete work/marks.json to redo)
marks_more: marking up further: {0} pieces of {1} already done, {2} batches ...
marks_done: headings {0}, running heads and numbers dropped {1}, breaks joined {2}
toc_found: contents: {0} chapters, {1} found in the text, {2} restored from it
toc_dropped: repeats dropped from headings as running heads, the first kept: {0}
h_wait: seconds to wait when rate-limited, 0 to fail instead (900 by default)
h_jobs: threads for editing and notes (translation is always sequential: each chunk builds on the previous one)
h_force_lang: translate even if the book is already in the target language
h_nohead: the book really has no chapters: do not stop at zero headings
h_partial: build the book even if translation is incomplete
h_encoding: input file encoding, when detection got it wrong (e.g. cp1251)
locked:
STOP: a run on this book is already in progress.
  Work directory {0} is held by process {1}.
  Wait for it or stop it, otherwise the chunks will overwrite each other.
scout_unfork: terms with two variants: {0} — picking one each ...
scout_forked: WARNING: the reference gives two variants for {0} terms. Pick one for each in work/scout.md, or the term will drift across the book:
no_summary: WARNING: the chunk came back without a digest. Check that the SUMMARY: and TERMS: labels in the translation prompt were not renamed: without them terminology will drift across the book.
refused: REFUSED: the model stopped twice at block {0}, leaving {1} of {2} untranslated. This is not a markup failure — it is the content of this passage:
refused_hint: Chunk skipped. Translate it with another model, naming its number:  --chunks {0} --agent claude  (what is done will not be paid for twice)
refused_row: STOPPED: {0} refusals in a row. This is no longer about the book: the model policy changed, the quota ran out, or the agent died. What is done is saved, and the next run picks it up.
refused_row_translate: This cannot be forced: translation is sequential and every chunk builds on the one before. Change the model, set a fallback — or name the remaining chunks yourself if the stubborn ones are to wait: --only translate --chunks 41-93
refused_row_edit: The chunk stays translated and readable, merely unedited. To keep editing regardless: --force-editing
h_fb_agent: agent for chunks the whole chain refused (older key; a colon inside the chain says it shorter)
h_fb_model: model for those chunks (older key; defaults to the translation model)
refused_both: the fallback models refused as well at block {0}; chunk skipped
bad_agent:
STOP: unknown agent "{0}". Available: {1}.
  Inside a model chain the agent goes before a colon: --editor model,claude:other-model
effort_clash:
STOP: agy takes the effort either as a model suffix or as --effort, never both.
  You gave: --model {0} and --effort {1}.
  Keep one: either «{0}», or the model without the suffix plus --effort {1}.
edit_failed: chunk {0} left unedited: no model of the chain took it
edit_stopped: WARNING: the edits stop at block {0} of {1}, with none after that. It looks like the editor did not finish the chunk — usually a sign of content the model will not handle. Worth re-editing with another model.
no_title: WARNING: no title in «{0}» was found — the book will keep its original title. Add a header to the instructions file:  ---  title_target: Your title  author_target: Author  ---
would_overwrite:
STOP: the output file would overwrite the source: {0}
  Give it another name with -o.
edits_unfinished: UNFINISHED EDITS — {0} chunks where editing broke off
edits_unfinished_item: chunk {0}: edits stop at block {1} of {2}
edits_unfinished_hint: They will not redo themselves: the file is written and resume counts them done. Re-edit with another model:  --only edit --chunks {0} --agent claude --model claude-opus-5
fail_wait: waiting {0} min after the failure, then the next chunk
no_backup: The chain holds one model — there is nothing to fall back to.
run_halted: Run stopped: the passes that follow call the same chain, and building a book with a hole would refuse anyway. What is done is saved, the next run picks it up.
qa2_spelled: numbers the language spells out ("in part one", "the eighties") do not count: {0} blocks
h_like: a book of the same cycle translated earlier: its names and terms go to the reconnaissance. Repeat the key; the order is the order of publication
reanchored: block numbering shifted: translation re-anchored, blocks: {}
h_name_series: include the cycle and book number in the output file name: “Author. Cycle 2. Title”
vf_done: DONE     author {0}, translation {1}, dismissed {2}, for a human {3}, in {4} s [{5}]
h_verifier: model chain for verifying editor remarks against the original (defaults to --editor)
